title: Maria Theresa Before the Hungarian Diet
text:
In 1740 the emperor Charles VI died, leaving his Habsburg lands to his twenty-three-year-old daughter, Maria Theresa. Almost immediately, Prussia invaded the rich province of Silesia, and France, Bavaria and Saxony moved against her. Her treasury was empty and her army weak. Her inheritance looked likely to be carved up.

She turned to Hungary, whose nobles had a long history of resisting Habsburg rule. On September 11, 1741, she appeared before the Hungarian Diet at Pressburg, now Bratislava. Speaking in Latin, the language of the Diet, she told them that her kingdom and her person were in danger, that she was abandoned by all, and that she placed herself in the hands of their loyalty and courage. Contemporary reports say she was in tears.

The nobles responded with a shout that became famous: "Vitam et sanguinem", their lives and blood for their king, Maria Theresa, using the title she held as crowned ruler of Hungary.

The Diet voted to raise troops. Behind the scene there had also been hard bargaining, and she confirmed Hungarian privileges, including the nobles' freedom from taxation. The Hungarian forces helped her hold her throne through the War of the Austrian Succession.
lesson: In a crisis, an honest appeal to people's honor and loyalty can win support that pressure never would, especially when backed by real concessions.
source: Contemporary reports from the Diet of Pressburg; records of the Hungarian Diet of 1741
caveat: The popular image of her holding up her infant son Joseph during this speech is an embellishment, since he was presented at a later session.
